findings.title: Completed response intentionally returns null lockdownMode
findings.description: AttemptMapper.toCompletedResponse() returns null for lockdownMode when the attempt is completed. This is intentional (completed attempts don't need lockdown state), but lacks explicit documentation.

evidence.snippet: return new AttemptTaskResponse(attempt.getPublicId(), attempt.getStatus().name(), true, null, null, null);

findings.impact: Minor: Developers reading this code may wonder if the null is intentional or a bug. The existing pattern (task=null, encryptionPublicKey=null) suggests this is by design, but lockdownMode's nullability isn't documented in AttemptTaskResponse's Javadoc.
findings.required_action: Add a Javadoc comment to AttemptTaskResponse explaining that lockdownMode is null when completed=true (similar to how task and encryptionPublicKey are already documented as context-dependent).

conventions_observed.naming: Java standard: PascalCase for classes/enums, camelCase for fields/methods
conventions_observed.dtos: Records for immutable DTOs; nullable fields represent 'not provided' in PATCH requests
conventions_observed.cross_service_serialization: String used for enum values crossing service boundaries (matches answerIntegrityLevel pattern)
conventions_observed.entity_fields: Nullable database columns with @PostLoad backfill for legacy data
conventions_observed.javadoc: Present on public APIs and domain models with architectural notes

notes: Phase 1 implementation follows existing patterns precisely. The lockdownMode field mirrors answerIntegrityLevel's architecture: enum in scheduling service, String in cross-service DTOs and pinned snapshots. No database migrations needed (Hibernate ddl-auto:update). No breaking changes. One LOW-severity advisory finding regarding documentation clarity; does not block phase completion.
